utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, over the break I consulted with my learned friend Mr. Krgovic. Save for this explanation, I have no further questions of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: We have no questions for this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, very short topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, can we just go over the sequence of events just to clarify to the Judges. You told us earlier that were detained in total 50 days; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ST-008
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Could you clarify to the Judges does that 50 days include your entire period of detention, including the police station, the TO, and Pribinic? Or is it something else?

utterances.speaker: ST-008
utterances.text: It includes the entire period. It lasted 50 days, including the TO, the station, and -- and Pribinic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: So this was starting the 3rd of June until somewhere in the middle of July, 50 days in total. Is that what we have to understand?

utterances.speaker: ST-008
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: That's all I ask, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: That concludes your testimony, sir. We are grateful for your assistance to the Tribunal. You are now released, and we wish you a safe journey back to your home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, we've been alerted that you have a matter that you wish to raise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I reviewed the list of documents marked for identification to see which ones were still missing translation. I would kindly ask that the next -- the following documents be removed from the MFI list. It is 2D32, 2D39, 2D40, 2D67, 2D122, 2D123, 2D124, 2D125. They were all previously MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have been given a list by Mr. Krgovic earlier this morning and but I would request an opportunity to check the transcripts and be sure that there wasn't some other objection that we had besides the fact that it was missing a translation and inform the Court of such objection, if any that we might have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we would defer a decision on that application until we next reconvene. And since you're on your feet, Mr. Hannis, where does the Office of the Prosecutor wish to take us from here?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I wanted to address that with you. We also have some marked for identification documents in e-court. We intended to file something in writing indicating which ones we sought to remove the MFI from and the reasons therefore. We know we're supposed to rest by Thursday this week. We don't have any other witnesses scheduled. We have a couple of matters pending with counsel to work out. Mr. Zecevic has proposed certain documents relating to Doboj be admitted and we can agree about some of those, the others we need to discuss. I would like to propose perhaps that we adjourn shortly and not resume before Wednesday and that will give us the time to discuss any of those matters we can resolve between ourselves. I think there are still perhaps a handful of pending motions that you have that we would like to have resolved before we finally and formally rest. And so that's my proposal, recess now until either witness or Thursday, to finally complete any remaining housekeeping matters and then rest later this week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, it goes without saying that those outstanding motions of which the Chamber is seized, we would have to dispose of before you formally close. But could you enlighten me as to what we would be -- for what purpose we would be reconvening on Wednesday as you propose.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Perhaps we don't have to reconvene until Thursday. I just said Wednesday out of an abundance of caution. If we realise that, oh, there are some serious matters that are going to take lengthy discussion or submissions or arguments before we can resolve them, to be sure that we can be done by Thursday. And that's the only reason I did it. Perhaps, since we do have space on the calendar, we can kind of keep that open, if something arises between now and the end of the day tomorrow that we need it, we can make use of it. If not, we'll just say okay, we'll meet on Thursday instead of Wednesday. That's my proposal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I see. There is a phrase which I find particularly useful which I owe to one of your countrymen who conducted a workshop in my country some years ago, and he warned against what he called Hello to the Judge meetings; that's what I'm trying to avoid. If we're going to do something, all well and good. So we adjourn ... so we take the adjournment to Wednesday morning. Does the Defence concur with that? Or, Mr. Demirdjian [sic] also suggested Thursday. Wednesday or Thursday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we believe Wednesday is fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So Wednesday morning at 9.00 in this courtroom. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 26th of January, 2011, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 12.45 p.m.,
